# Baseline UI: de-slop interface polish rules

Curated by Skill Harbor — @ibelick's baseline UI skill (Ibelick is known for polished interface taste): an opinionated constraint set that prevents AI-generated interface slop. Two modes — apply the constraints to any UI work in the conversation (`/baseline-ui`), or audit a file against all constraints and get back violations (quoted line), why it matters, and a concrete code-level fix. The rules are specific: Tailwind CSS defaults, motion/react for JS animation, accessible primitives (Base UI, React Aria, Radix — never rebuilt by hand, never mixed within one surface), AlertDialog for destructive actions, errors next to the action, animate only compositor props and never beyond 200ms for feedback, text-balance/text-pretty typography, fixed z-index scale, no gradients, no purple/multicolor gradients, no glow effects, one accent color per view. Honest caveat: opinionated on purpose — it will fight you if your design system genuinely needs gradients, heavy animation or custom easing; treat it as a cleanup pass, not a design identity. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
